data.name: RAZED
data.detailed_description:
"RAZED é um rapidíssimo jogo de corridas em plataformas para um jogador, onde a velocidade é rainha.
Acelera o mais rápido que conseguires por níveis dinâmicos em tons de néon, graças a poderes como supervelocidade, mega saltos, drifts, estrondos e desvios para contornar obstáculos e encontrar atalhos que te levem ao topo das classificações online. Mas nem tudo é simples: os poderes custam impulso e se ficares com pouca energia tanto tu como os teus sapatos poderão, bem, explodir...



A INTENSIDADE NÃO DÁ DESCANSO
Acelera por 60 níveis dinâmicos através de seis mundos únicos, cada um deles com um estilo visual peculiar, poderes para desbloqueares e combates com bosses incrivelmente intensos.

CRIA O TEU PRÓPRIO PERCURSO
Faz desvios invulgares e cria o teu próprio caminho pelos níveis para fazer tempos impossíveis e desbloquear as classificações S.

CLASSIFICAÇÕES ONLINE E DADOS FANTASMA
Desafia todo o mundo nas classificações online e enfrenta os fantasmas dos teus amigos num desafio de superação assíncrona.

SPEEDRUNNING SEM CHATICES
Ninguém quer ficar à espera quando busca a perfeição. Estás longe do recorde que persegues? Prime o botão de reinício para voltar ao início do nível sem ficar à espera do tempo de carregamento.

NÍVEIS DE DESAFIO SECRETOS
Usa todos os teus poderes para encontrar e enfrentar os mapas mais desafiantes de RAZED."

reviews.review:
RAZED is an arcade-focused 3D platformer that treats movement itself as a race. Developed by Warpfish Games and published by PQube, it revolves around completing compact obstacle courses at increasingly ridiculous speeds. Rather than encouraging players to carefully explore every corner, the game constantly pushes them forward. Every jump, turn, shortcut, and ability becomes part of the pursuit of a faster completion time, creating an experience that feels somewhere between a precision platformer and a time-trial racing game.

The defining mechanic is the player's momentum. Moving quickly keeps the run alive, while losing too much speed can have explosive consequences thanks to the character's volatile footwear. This simple concept gives every level a natural sense of urgency. Even stretches that initially appear straightforward become challenging when approached at full speed. Players must simultaneously watch the terrain ahead, maintain momentum, avoid hazards, and prepare for the next jump without having much time to reconsider a decision.

Progression gradually expands the movement system with abilities such as powerful jumps, speed boosts, strafing, drifting, and stomping. These mechanics turn later stages into considerably more complicated tests of timing and resource management. Special abilities consume momentum, so repeatedly activating them without thinking is rarely an effective strategy. Successful runs depend on learning exactly where an ability provides the greatest advantage and where maintaining natural speed is the safer option. This creates a satisfying balance between aggressive movement and controlled execution.

The campaign contains 60 levels spread across six worlds, giving the game enough environmental variety to keep its central concept interesting. Each world develops the challenge further while introducing new abilities and eventually testing players through boss encounters. The presentation embraces a colorful, neon-heavy arcade aesthetic that fits the frantic movement extremely well. Environments are designed to remain visually readable at high speeds, although the sheer pace can occasionally make upcoming hazards difficult to process during an unfamiliar run.

Level design becomes more interesting once players stop treating the obvious path as the only path. Alternative routes and shortcuts are an important part of improving completion times. Simply reaching the end is therefore only the beginning. Returning to a stage with greater knowledge of its layout can reveal opportunities to skip sections, preserve momentum, or approach obstacles differently. Chasing the highest rankings transforms short stages into puzzles about efficiency, where understanding the route can be almost as important as having quick reflexes.

The instant restart system is particularly valuable. Mistakes are inevitable in a game built around precision and speed, but failed attempts rarely create substantial downtime. A bad jump or poorly timed ability can quickly be followed by another attempt, preserving the rhythm of play. This makes repeated failure much easier to tolerate and encourages experimentation. It is easy to tell yourself that the next attempt will be the successful one, only to spend considerably longer refining a route than originally intended.

Online leaderboards and ghost racing provide another layer of motivation. Players can compare completion times and use ghost data as a reference when trying to understand how much faster a course can be completed. These systems suit the game's competitive nature without requiring conventional multiplayer. There are also hidden challenge levels that place greater demands on the movement abilities acquired throughout the campaign. Combined with achievements, rankings, shortcuts, and personal best times, these features give dedicated players plenty of reasons to revisit earlier content.

The biggest limitation is also part of the game's identity. RAZED is extremely focused on speedrunning. Players looking for extensive storytelling, open exploration, elaborate character progression, or a relaxed platforming adventure will find comparatively little of that here. The repeated process of failing, restarting, memorizing layouts, and improving times is fundamental to the experience. Later challenges can become unforgiving, especially when a good run is ruined by one mistimed jump or poor landing.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently best considered unverified rather than officially confirmed as Verified or Playable. The game's relatively lightweight technical requirements and controller-oriented arcade design make it conceptually well suited to handheld play, but an official Steam Deck compatibility rating should not be assumed. Individual results may therefore depend on the current Proton version, configuration, and any updates made to the game or SteamOS.

RAZED ultimately delivers a concentrated form of arcade platforming where improvement is the real reward. Its responsive movement concepts, momentum management, quick restarts, shortcuts, rankings, ghost competition, and progressively more demanding courses create an addictive loop for anyone who enjoys mastering mechanics rather than simply reaching the credits. It can be punishing and intentionally repetitive, but that repetition has purpose because nearly every restart offers another opportunity to execute the route more cleanly. For players attracted to precision platforming and speedrunning, it offers a compact challenge with considerably more replay value than its straightforward premise initially suggests.

Rating: 7/10
